artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_.title: Signed Provenance Verified on Artifact Admission
artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_.description: Attests that the deploying environment cryptographically verifies a SLSA provenance attestation (or equivalent signed in-toto attestation) on every artifact before admission, with the signature chained to a pinned builder identity, OIDC issuer, and expected source repo/ref — never admitting an artifact pulled by tag alone. When false, the channel will accept tampered or substituted artifacts (SLSA bypass).

commits_signed.title: Commits on Deploy Ref Are Signed
commits_signed.description: Attestation: every commit on the deploy ref is cryptographically signed (GPG, SSH, S/MIME, or keyless Sigstore/gitsign) and verified. Insecure (false) when recent commits on the deploy ref show 'no signature' under `git log --show-signature`. Secure value: true.

required_signatures_enforced_on_deploy_r.title: Required-Signatures Rule Enforced on Deploy Ref
required_signatures_enforced_on_deploy_r.description: Attestation: the repository ruleset / branch protection on the deploy ref enforces the `required_signatures` rule (integrity change control), so unsigned commits are rejected at push time rather than relying on contributor discipline. Insecure (false) when no `required_signatures` entry is present under `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/rules/branches/<deploy-ref>`. Secure value: true.

cicd_pipeline_identity_per_environment_n.title: Per-Environment Short-Lived CI/CD Identity
cicd_pipeline_identity_per_environment_n.description: Attestation that the CI/CD pipeline authenticates to each target environment with a distinct, short-lived, federated workload identity (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC pinned by sub/audience to repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env>, federated to per-environment cloud roles) rather than a single long-lived static cloud credential shared across all environments. True when every environment has a separate OIDC-federated identity with environment-scoped trust pins AND no long-lived org-wide cloud key sits in repo secrets; false when a shared static credential authenticates deploys to multiple environments — a single token leak collapses blast radius to every environment at once.

deploy_ref_protected_branch_only.title: Deploy Restricted to Protected Branch/Tag
deploy_ref_protected_branch_only.description: Attests that the deploy workflow / environment is gated so it can only fire from a protected branch (or protected tag) — i.e. GitHub environment deployment_branch_policy.protected_branches=true, or an equivalent ref restriction in the CI platform. When false, a push to any branch (including a fork PR) can drive the deploy flow.

deploy_required_reviewers_configured.title: Required Human Reviewers on Deploy
deploy_required_reviewers_configured.description: Attests that the deployment environment (e.g. prod) has required human reviewers configured as an environment protection rule — so a deploy cannot proceed without explicit approval, even from a protected branch. When false, the channel runs unattended on every qualifying push.

secrets_injected_at_runtime_not_baked_in.title: Secrets Injected at Runtime (Not Baked)
secrets_injected_at_runtime_not_baked_in.description: Attests that secrets traversing the deployment channel are injected into the running workload at deploy/start time from an external secret store (Vault Agent, Secrets-Store CSI, External Secrets Operator) — never embedded in the image, ConfigMap, Dockerfile, or build artifact carried by the flow. When false, credentials baked into the artifact ride the channel into every environment.

secret_scanning_enabled.title: Blocking Secret Scanner on Artifact and Manifests
secret_scanning_enabled.description: Attests that the deploy pipeline runs a blocking secret scanner (gitleaks, trufflehog, trivy --scanners secret, detect-secrets) on the artifact AND on rendered Helm/Kustomize manifests before applying — catching credentials that slipped past commit-time hooks. When false, embedded secrets traverse the flow undetected.

flow_tls_encrypted.title: Deploy Channel Carried Over TLS End-to-End
flow_tls_encrypted.description: Attestation: the deployment channel (registry pull, kube-apiserver call, GitOps webhook) is carried over TLS 1.2+ end-to-end with no cleartext fallback. False fires the exposure: cleartext or downgraded transport on the deploy flow opens classic MITM artifact substitution.

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Strictly Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Attestation: the deploying client strictly validates the server certificate (trusted CA chain, SAN match, no self-signed acceptance) on every connection in the deploy flow. False fires the exposure: accepting self-signed or unvalidated TLS lets an on-path attacker terminate the channel and substitute the artifact or deploy verb.

artifact_references_immutable_digest_pin.title: Artifacts Referenced by Immutable Digest
artifact_references_immutable_digest_pin.description: Attestation that every manifest crossing this deployment flow references its artifact by immutable digest (sha256:...) rather than a mutable tag (:latest, :prod, :stable). When false, the registry can repoint the tag to a different (malicious) digest after admission-time verification, so pods restarting later pull a substituted image under the same tag — what policy verified is no longer what runs.

centralized_log_aggregation.title: Deploy Events Streamed to Central Aggregator
centralized_log_aggregation.description: Attests that deploy events crossing this flow are streamed to a central, out-of-account audit log/SIEM (true) — when false, deploy events never reach a tamper-evident aggregator and post-incident attribution is guesswork.

audit_log_tamper_evident.title: Audit Log Destination Tamper-Evident
audit_log_tamper_evident.description: Attests that the audit log destination is tamper-evident — write-once / append-only / cryptographically chained, hosted in an account the deploying identity cannot edit (true). When false, an attacker with cluster-admin or the deploy identity can erase their tracks even if logs are forwarded.

drift_detection_enabled.title: Continuous Drift Detection Enabled
drift_detection_enabled.description: Attests that the deployment flow runs continuous reconciliation (GitOps controller such as Argo CD selfHeal / Flux, or terraform plan -detailed-exitcode wired to alerts) against a declared source-of-truth, so any out-of-band change to running config is detected and alerted. Insecure value (false) fires this exposure: out-of-band kubectl/console changes go unnoticed.

running_config_matches_baseline.title: Running Config Matches Declared Baseline
running_config_matches_baseline.description: Attests that, at assessment time, the running configuration of the target environment is in sync with the declared source-of-truth baseline (argocd app diff / flux diff / terraform plan reports no differences). Insecure value (false) fires this exposure: drift is currently present and persisting because no reconciliation evicted it.
